name: Selection Sort
description: Repeatedly selects the minimum element from the unsorted portion and swaps it to the front. Makes only O(n) swaps, which is its main advantage over Bubble Sort.
aim: Sort an array by finding the minimum element from the unsorted region and moving it to its correct position, extending the sorted region one element per pass.
howItWorks: Scan unsorted region to find minimum element
Swap minimum with first element of unsorted region
Repeat until unsorted region is empty

time.bestCase: Always n(n-1)/2 comparisons — no early exit
time.averageCase: Same comparisons regardless of input order

realWorld: Useful when memory writes are costly — only O(n) swaps made
Embedded systems requiring predictable comparison counts
Small datasets where simplicity beats performance
whenToUse: When minimizing memory writes matters more than comparisons
Simple in-place sort needed with no stability requirement
alternatives: Insertion Sort — better on nearly-sorted data (adaptive)
Quick Sort — O(n log n) average for large data
Bubble Sort — similar complexity but more swaps
